extracted.intended_audience: journalists and news organizations (reporters, editors, newsrooms) considering submitting to the George Polk Awards
extracted.subtask_description: Submit nominations/entries for the George Polk Awards, a journalism prize that emphasizes investigative and enterprise reporting; includes eligibility, categories, language and fee requirements and the deadline. Useful for reporters, editors, and news organizations preparing entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judging preference: investigative and enterprise work
rubrics_metrics.description: Judges place a premium on investigative and enterprise work that is original, requires digging and resourcefulness, and brings results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries should demonstrate originality, substantial reporting effort ('digging'), resourcefulness in uncovering information, and tangible results or impacts stemming from the reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible media/outlets
rubrics_metrics.description: Winners are chosen from newspapers, magazines, television, radio and online news organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions may come from traditional and digital outlets across these media types; the award is not restricted to a single platform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic/nationality eligibility and language
rubrics_metrics.description: While the journalists or media outlet do not have to be American, all entries must be in English (no translations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: International work is eligible provided the entry is submitted in English; translated pieces are not accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories and formats considered
rubrics_metrics.description: Categories vary from year to year, but it has been customary to give awards in foreign, national and local reporting (in print and broadcasting), business and environmental reporting and photojournalism. Electronic journalism, documentary films and books based on investigative reporting or dealing specifically with the field of journalism also may be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitters should check current-year categories but may propose work across a broad set of formats including print, broadcast, online, photojournalism, electronic journalism, documentaries and investigative books.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nomination and selection process
rubrics_metrics.description: Nominees are proposed and selected by a national panel of advisors. The panel also considers entries that originate from publication offices, newsrooms or individual reporters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries may be submitted by organizations or individuals; selection is made by a national advisory panel rather than by public vote.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry fee
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include payment of the $75 fee with a submission as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission deadline
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries must be submitted by the stated date to be considered for that year's awards.
